deployment.title: Deploy Collectors
deployment.description: Run the command on any number of hosts — they enroll into the fleet you pick and appear as they check in.
deployment.tokens_description: Tokens authorize new Collectors to enroll into a fleet. Deleting a token does not affect already-enrolled Collectors.

fleets.title: Fleets
fleets.description: A fleet is a group of collectors that share the same configuration. All collectors in a fleet collect data from the same sources. Use fleets to organize collectors by environment, team, or purpose.

instances.title: Instances
instances.description: A collector instance represents a running collector process on a remote host. Instances enroll into a fleet using an enrollment token and automatically receive their fleet's source configuration.

onboarding.title: Collector Onboarding
onboarding.description: Status of your newly connected collector.
onboarding.not_found: Collector instance not found. It may have been removed — see all <instancesLink>Instances</instancesLink>.

overview.title: Collectors Overview
overview.description: Collectors are lightweight services deployed across your infrastructure to collect logs and forward them to {{productName}}. They are organized into fleets and configured with sources that define what data to collect.

settings.title: Collectors Settings
settings.description: Configure the endpoints and lifecycle settings for managed collectors. Collectors connect to these endpoints to receive configuration updates and send collected log data.

settings.getting_started_cloud: Collectors connect to a managed ingest endpoint to send their data. Save your collector settings to initialize the collector infrastructure. After setup, you can create fleets, add sources, and deploy collectors to your hosts.
settings.getting_started_self_managed: Collectors need ingest endpoints to receive collected data. Configure the HTTP endpoint below and save to initialize the collector infrastructure. After setup, you can create fleets, add sources, and deploy collectors to your hosts.
settings.ingest_endpoint_cloud: The ingest endpoint is system-managed. Collectors connect here automatically.
settings.ingest_endpoint_help: Ingest endpoints receive log data from collectors via OpenTelemetry (OTLP). The external address that is pushed to managed collectors as their data destination. It must route to a running collector ingest input. This is typically the address of a load balancer or the server itself.
settings.hostname_help: The hostname or IP address that Collectors will use to connect. Must be reachable from Collector hosts.
settings.offline_threshold_help: Collectors that haven't reported within this time are shown as offline.
settings.default_visibility_help: Collectors that haven't reported within this time are hidden from the default view. Users can adjust or remove this filter in the instances table.
settings.expiration_threshold_help: Collectors that haven't reported within this time are permanently removed.

source_form.max_poll_interval_error: Max poll interval must be at least 1 seconds.
source_form.max_log_age_error: Max log age must be 0 or a positive value.
source_form.file_paths_help: Glob patterns supported (e.g., /var/log/*.log, /var/log/**/*.log). The Collector watches matched files for new lines.
source_form.read_mode_file_help: From end: only collect new lines after the Collector starts. From beginning: collect all existing lines first, then continue tailing.
source_form.read_mode_journald_help: From end: only collect new entries after the Collector starts. From beginning: collect all existing entries first, then continue tailing.
source_form.priority_help: Minimum severity level to collect. For example, selecting Error also collects Critical, Alert, and Emergency entries.
source_form.match_pattern_help: Optional journald match expression to filter entries by unit, process, etc. Example: _SYSTEMD_UNIT=nginx.service
source_form.channels_help: Comma-separated channel names (e.g., Application, Security, System)
source_form.predicate_help: Optional macOS unified logging filter predicate passed to the log command. Leaving this empty collects all logs from the system! info or debug levels are not currently collected, as they are very noisy and carry very little valuable information. Example: {{example}}
source_form.max_poll_interval_help: How often the Collector checks for new log entries. Must be at least 1 second.
source_form.max_log_age_help: On first start, how far back to backfill logs. Set to 0 to disable backfilling.
source_form.description: A source defines what data Collectors in this fleet should collect. Each source type corresponds to a different collection method.
source_form.file_type_help: Collect log lines from files on the host. Supports glob patterns for matching multiple files.
source_form.journald_type_help: Collect entries from the systemd journal (Linux only).
source_form.windows_type_help: Collect events from Windows Event Viewer channels.
source_form.macos_type_help: Collect from the macOS unified logging system via the log command (macOS only).
source_form.enabled_help: Disabled sources are not sent to Collectors. Use this to temporarily stop collection without removing the source.
